entities.name: Zipoetes II of Bithynia
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Zipoetes II of Bithynia was a short-lived but significant ruler of Bithynia from 279 BCE to 276 BCE. His name, which survives chiefly in Hellenized forms, has three syllables.


As the successor of his father Zipoetes I, Zipoetes II played a crucial role in maintaining Bithynia's independence from the expanding Roman Empire. Despite his limited time in power, Zipoetes II successfully defended Bithynia against Roman aggression and even forced the Romans to withdraw from the region.


Zipoetes II's legacy extends beyond his military victories, as he also established a period of cultural and economic prosperity in Bithynia. His reign saw the rise of Bithynian art, architecture, and trade, which had a lasting impact on the development of the region.


The exact dates of Zipoetes II's birth and death are unknown, but his impact on the history of Bithynia and the Roman Empire cannot be overstated. He remains one of the most fascinating and enigmatic figures of the ancient world.


In the end, Zipoetes II's bravery and cunning allowed Bithynia to maintain its independence for a short time, but ultimately, the region fell to the Romans in 74 BCE.
